messages.subject: Re: Multi-threaded usage
messages.body_plain:
Hi Vladimir,
Yes! Renjin is very much designed to run in a multi-threaded environment. You should start a new Session or ScriptEngine for each thread however, as many packages and base R functions interact with session-level state. Vectors (including data.frame objects for example) can be safely shared between multiple ScriptEngine instances.

You may also want to exercise more control over Renjin's implicit parallelization: if you may want all sessions to share a common thread pool, or limit each session to a single thread. This can be done by using Renjin's own SessionBuilder, see
https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/blob/master/cli/src/main/java/org/renjin/cli/Main.java#L146

for an example of providing your own ThreadPool instance.

Let us know how it turns out!

Best,
Alex

messages.subject: Problem executing R functions from JAVA
messages.subject_clean: Problem executing R functions from JAVA
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
 I am facing an issue while connecting to R from JAVA using Renjin.

I have downloaded the "renjin-script-engine-0.7.1578-jar-with-dependencies" and its working fine.
I have successfully calculated standard deviation,mean,etc of a vector from Java using R functions.

But I am getting an error while calculating the correlation of 2 vectors using function "cor" .
Here is the error:

Exception in thread "main" java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: java/util/Objects

What do I do??
Do I need any CRAN package in Renjin??
If so how do I implement??

I have even tried loading the library by
engine.eval("library('org.renjin.cran:corrplot')");

Still I am getting an error
Exception in thread "main" org.renjin.eval.EvalException: Could not load package org.renjin.cran:corrplot; tried org.renjin.cran:corrplot, org.renjin.bioconductor:org.renjin.cran:corrplot, org.renjin.cran:org.renjin.cran:corrplot

So I how do I implement the correlation function of R in Java and how do I make sure I have access to all other R functions using Rengine in JAVA??

And my main goal is to use R functions in Java without actually installing R in my computer.

A quick reply will be highly appreciated.

Thank You,
Rajib Roy.
